info.title: Gig Maestro — Bitwig Studio RPC API
info.description:
Control Bitwig Studio programmatically via JSON-RPC 2.0. All methods are invoked as POST requests to a single endpoint (`/rpc`). This spec models each RPC method as its own path for interactive documentation. In practice, all requests go to `POST /rpc` with the method name in the JSON body.

**HTTP Endpoint:** `POST http://localhost:8787/rpc`

**WebSocket Endpoint:** `ws://localhost:8788/` (real-time state streaming)

**Protocol:** JSON-RPC 2.0

post.summary: Retrieve the full current state of the Bitwig Studio session.
post.description: Retrieve the full current state of the Bitwig Studio session. Returns transport state (playing, tempo, position, metronomeVolume, preRoll), all tracks (name, volume, pan, mute, solo, arm, isMutedBySolo, sends, crossfadeMode, monitorMode, trackType, isGroup, isGroupExpanded, canHoldNoteData, canHoldAudioData), master track (volume, pan, mute, solo, color), project state (hasSoloedTracks, hasMutedTracks, hasArmedTracks, isModified, panelLayout), clip grid (64 tracks x 8 slots with content, playback, and recording states), scenes, device state (cursor track, cursor device, remote control parameters with hasAutomation flag, nesting info: isNested, hasSlots, slotNames, hasLayers, hasDrumPads), masterDevice state (master bus device chain, parameters, nesting info), application state (project name, undo/redo), arranger state (7 visibility toggles), arrangement state (loop range, punch in/out, automation mode, cue markers), browser state (exists, title, selectedContentType, contentTypeNames, canAudition, shouldAudition, resultName, resultIsSelected, resultsEntryCount, filters with 8 columns: category/tag/creator/device/deviceType/fileType/location/smartCollection each with exists/name/hitCount/entryCount), arpeggiator state (isEnabled, mode, octaves, rate, gateLength, shuffle, humanize, isFreeRunning, enableOverlappingNotes, usePressureToVelocity, terminateNotesImmediately), noteLatch state (isEnabled, mode, mono, velocityThreshold, activeNotes), and groove state (enabled, shuffleAmount, shuffleRate, accentAmount, accentRate, accentPhase). Always call this before taking actions to understand the current state, and after actions to verify results.

post.summary: Touch or untouch a remote control parameter for automation recording.
post.description: Touch or untouch a remote control parameter for automation recording. When touched during playback with automation write enabled, parameter value changes are recorded to the automation lane. Always untouch after recording to stop capturing changes. WARNING: Forgetting to untouch leaves the parameter in recording mode.

index.description: Parameter index on the current page (0-based). Valid range: 0 to 7.

touched.description: True to enter touch/recording mode, false to exit.

post.summary: Write an automation envelope curve for a remote control parameter.
post.description: Write an automation envelope curve for a remote control parameter. Takes an array of {position, value} points and records them as automation data in the arranger. Internally uses simulated touch recording with playback — returns immediately but recording completes asynchronously (~100ms per point). PREREQUISITES: (1) Arranger automation write must be enabled via `transport_setArrangerAutomationWrite`. (2) Automation write mode should be set (e.g., 'touch' via `transport_setAutomationWriteMode`). Transport position and play/stop state are saved and restored after recording. Points are sorted by position, values clamped to [0,1], duplicate positions use last-wins.

index.description: Parameter index on the current page (0-based). Valid range: 0 to 7.

points.description: Array of automation points to write. Points are sorted by position automatically.

position.description: Beat position in the arranger (must be >= 0).

value.description: Parameter value, normalized 0.0 to 1.0. Values outside this range are clamped.

post.summary: Navigate the cursor track selection to the next or previous track sequentially.

direction.description: Direction to move the cursor: 'next' for the track below, 'previous' for the track above.

post.summary: Delete a clip from a clip launcher slot.
post.description: Delete a clip from a clip launcher slot. Removes the clip and its contents entirely.

slotIndex.description: Clip slot index (0-based). Valid range: 0 to 7.

post.summary: Select a clip slot for note editing.
post.description: Select a clip slot for note editing. The cursor clip will follow this selection, making it the target for setNotes, getNotes, clearNote, and clearAllNotes. Must be called before editing notes in a specific clip. IMPORTANT: Cursor movement is async — after selecting, wait 1-2 seconds before calling getNotes to allow step data to load. Writing (setNotes) uses deferred scheduling and is not affected.

slotIndex.description: Clip slot index (0-based). Valid range: 0 to 7.

post.summary: Write multiple notes into the selected clip in a single batch operation.
post.description: Write multiple notes into the selected clip in a single batch operation. Each note is placed at a grid position (x=step, y=MIDI note). Existing notes at the same positions are overwritten. Use this to write entire patterns, chords, basslines, or drum sequences in one call.

notes.description: Array of notes to write. Each note has x (step position), y (MIDI note number), velocity (0.0-1.0, optional, default ~0.79), and duration (in beats, optional, default 0.25). To set note probability, use clip_setChance after writing notes (chance requires a separate call due to Bitwig's flush cycle).

x.description: Step position in the grid (0-based). At 1/16 resolution: 0-15 = bar 1, 16-31 = bar 2, etc.

y.description: MIDI note number (0-127). Common values: 36=C2 (kick), 38=D2 (snare), 42=F#2 (hi-hat), 60=C4 (middle C).

velocity.description: Note velocity, 0.0 (silent) to 1.0 (maximum). Optional, defaults to ~0.79.

duration.description: Note duration in beats. 0.25 = 1/16 note, 0.5 = 1/8 note, 1.0 = 1/4 note. Optional, defaults to 0.25.

post.summary: Remove a single note at the specified grid position in the selected clip.
post.description: Remove a single note at the specified grid position in the selected clip.

post.summary: Remove all notes from the selected clip.
post.description: Remove all notes from the selected clip. This clears the entire clip content.

post.summary: Read all notes in the selected clip's current grid viewport.
post.description: Read all notes in the selected clip's current grid viewport. Returns a sparse array containing only cells with notes (NoteOn state). Each note includes x (step), y (MIDI note), velocity (0.0-1.0), duration (beats), and expressive properties when non-default: pan (-1..1), timbre (-1..1), pressure (0..1), gain (0..1, 0.5=0dB), transpose (-96..+96 semitones), releaseVelocity (0..1), velocitySpread (0..1), mute (boolean), chance (0..1), occurrence (NoteOccurrence enum string), recurrence ({length, mask}), repeat ({count, curve, velocityEnd, velocityCurve}). IMPORTANT: After clip/select, wait 1-2 seconds before calling this — the cursor clip loads step data asynchronously, and reading too soon returns empty or stale results.

post.summary: Set the probability (chance) for existing notes in the selected clip.
post.description: Set the probability (chance) for existing notes in the selected clip. Notes must already exist — call clip_setNotes first, then clip_setChance. Each entry specifies the step position (x, y) and the chance value. When chance is enabled, the note only plays with the given probability on each loop iteration.

notes.description: Array of note positions with chance values.

x.description: Step position of the existing note.

y.description: MIDI note number of the existing note.

chance.description: Probability the note plays (0.0 to 1.0). 0.5 = 50% chance, 1.0 = always plays.

post.summary: Set expressive properties on existing notes in the selected clip.
post.description: Set expressive properties on existing notes in the selected clip. Batch-set scalar note properties like pan, timbre, pressure, gain, transpose, releaseVelocity, velocitySpread, or mute. Each entry targets a specific note by step position (x, y) and sets one property at a time. Notes must already exist. Call after clip_setNotes.

x.description: Step position of the existing note.

y.description: MIDI note number of the existing note.

property.description: Property to set. One of: pan (-1..1), timbre (-1..1), pressure (0..1), gain (0..1, 0.5=0dB), transpose (-96..+96), releaseVelocity (0..1), velocitySpread (0..1), mute (0=unmute, non-zero=mute).

value.description: Value to set for the property. Range depends on property.

post.summary: Set note repeat (note echo/ratchet) properties on existing notes.
post.description: Set note repeat (note echo/ratchet) properties on existing notes. Enables repeat and sets all 4 sub-properties together. Repeat creates rhythmic subdivisions of a note — positive count = divisions, negative count = rate. Notes must already exist.

notes.description: Array of notes with repeat settings.

x.description: Step position of the existing note.

y.description: MIDI note number of the existing note.

count.description: Repeat count (-127..127). Positive = number of divisions, negative = rate.

curve.description: Timing curve (-1..1). 0 = linear, negative = accelerating, positive = decelerating.

velocityEnd.description: Velocity change over repeats (-1..1). Relative amount applied to note velocity.

velocityCurve.description: Velocity curve shape (-1..1). 0 = linear velocity change.

post.summary: Set occurrence conditions on existing notes.
post.description: Set occurrence conditions on existing notes. Occurrence controls when a note plays based on context: whether it's the first time, whether previous notes were playing, fill mode, etc. Notes must already exist.

notes.description: Array of notes with occurrence conditions.

x.description: Step position of the existing note.

y.description: MIDI note number of the existing note.

post.summary: Set recurrence patterns on existing notes.
post.description: Set recurrence patterns on existing notes. Recurrence makes notes play only on specific iterations of a cycle (1-8 steps). The mask is a bitmask where bit N controls whether the note plays on cycle N. Example: length=4, mask=5 (binary 0101) = plays on cycles 1 and 3. Notes must already exist.

notes.description: Array of notes with recurrence patterns.

x.description: Step position of the existing note.

y.description: MIDI note number of the existing note.

mask.description: Bitmask for which cycles the note plays. Bit N = cycle N. Max 8 bits.

post.summary: Set the step grid resolution for the cursor clip.
post.description: Set the step grid resolution for the cursor clip. This determines the time duration of each step in the grid. Common values: 0.25 = 1/16 note (default), 0.5 = 1/8 note, 1.0 = 1/4 note, 0.125 = 1/32 note.

post.summary: Scroll the step grid viewport to a specific step offset.
post.description: Scroll the step grid viewport to a specific step offset. The grid viewport is 64 steps wide. Use this to navigate to different sections of clips longer than 64 steps. Offset 0 = beginning, 64 = second page, etc.

offset.description: Step offset to scroll to (0-based). The viewport will show 64 steps starting from this position.

post.summary: Insert a built-in Bitwig device onto the cursor track by name.
post.description: Insert a built-in Bitwig device onto the cursor track by name. The name is resolved case-insensitively from the Bitwig device library (151 devices). If the name is not found, an error is returned with close-match suggestions. Use `device_listBitwigDevices` to discover available devices first.

position.description: Where to insert: "end" = end of device chain (default), "before" = before cursor device, "after" = after cursor device.

post.summary: Insert a third-party plugin (VST2, VST3, or CLAP) onto the cursor track.
post.description: Insert a third-party plugin (VST2, VST3, or CLAP) onto the cursor track. You must know the plugin ID — VST2 uses integer IDs, VST3 and CLAP use string IDs.

id.description: Plugin ID. For VST2: integer as string (e.g., "1234567890"). For VST3/CLAP: string ID.

position.description: Where to insert: "end" = end of device chain (default), "before" = before cursor device, "after" = after cursor device.

post.summary: List all available built-in Bitwig devices.
post.description: List all available built-in Bitwig devices. Returns a sorted array of device names that can be used with `device_insertBitwigDevice`. Includes instruments (Polymer, Poly Grid, FM-4, etc.), audio effects (EQ-5, Compressor, Delay-2, etc.), and note effects (Arpeggiator, Note Echo, etc.).

post.summary: Remove the currently selected device from the cursor track's device chain.
post.description: Remove the currently selected device from the cursor track's device chain. Navigate to the target device first using `device_selectNext` / `device_selectPrevious`, then call this to delete it. Warning: the cursor device loses selection after removal — call `session_snapshot` to verify state. This action cannot be undone via this API (but Bitwig's undo may work).

post.summary: Returns the drum pad names and their MIDI note numbers for the currently selected device.
post.description: Returns the drum pad names and their MIDI note numbers for the currently selected device. Only works when the device has drum pads (hasDrumPads: true in snapshot). Use this to discover which MIDI note corresponds to which drum sound (e.g., kick, snare, hi-hat) before writing notes with clip_setNotes. post.summary: Execute a sequence of RPC operations atomically with stop-on-error semantics.
post.description: Execute a sequence of RPC operations atomically with stop-on-error semantics. Each operation is executed sequentially — if any step fails, execution stops immediately and partial results are returned. Use this to batch dependent calls (e.g., create clip then select it) where later steps should not run if earlier steps fail. Optionally capture state snapshots before and/or after execution, and optionally roll back completed steps on error via app/undo.

operations.description: Ordered list of RPC operations to execute. Each operation has a 'method' (RPC method name like 'clip/create') and optional 'params' (method parameters).

params.description: Parameters for the RPC method. Defaults to empty object if omitted.

preSnapshot.description: If true, capture a full state snapshot before executing any operations. Returned in the response as 'preSnapshot'. Default: false.

postSnapshot.description: If true, capture a full state snapshot after all operations complete (or after the last successful step on error). Returned in the response as 'postSnapshot'. Default: false.

rollback.description: If set to 'undoAll' and an error occurs, call app/undo N times for N successfully completed steps (best-effort). The response includes rollback info: { rolledBack: true, undoCount: N }.

post.summary: Create a new track with optional rename, color, device insertion, and sound design in a single call.
post.description: Create a new track with optional rename, color, device insertion, and sound design in a single call. Composes track/create + track/rename + track/setColor + device/insertBitwigDevice + macro/createSound. Use instead of calling these methods separately.

name.description: Name to assign to the new track. If omitted, the track keeps its default name.

position.description: 0-based insert position. -1 or omitted = append at end.

device.description: Name of a Bitwig built-in device to insert on the new track (e.g., 'Polymer', 'Drum Machine'). Case-insensitive. Mutually exclusive with 'plugin'.

plugin.description: Third-party plugin device to insert. Mutually exclusive with 'device'.

id.description: Plugin identifier. VST2: numeric string. VST3: GUID string. CLAP: reverse-domain string (e.g., 'com.vendor.synth').

color.description: Track color as RGB floats (0.0 to 1.0). Applied after rename, before device insertion.

pages.description: Parameter pages to apply to the inserted device (requires 'device'). Same format as macro/createSound pages. Device parameters are set after a flush cycle to allow initialization.

params.description: Parameters to set on this page.

index.description: Parameter index within the page (0-7).

post.description: Create an empty clip and select it (cursor clip ready for note writing) in a single call. Composes clip/create + clip/select. Use instead of calling these 2 methods separately.

lengthBeats.description: Clip length in beats (e.g., 16 for 4 bars in 4/4).

Returns { count } with the number of notes (optimistic — note writes are deferred to next flush cycle). To verify notes were actually written, call clip/getNotes after a 1-2 second delay.

lengthBeats.description: Clip length in beats (e.g., 16 for 4 bars in 4/4).

notes.description: Array of note objects to write.

expressions.description: Per-note expression values. Each key is a property name, value is 0.0–1.0.

mask.description: Bitmask for active steps in cycle.

post.description: Build a song section: create/rename a scene and write clips across multiple tracks. If sceneIndex is provided, uses that existing scene slot directly (recommended after manual scene creation or bulk deletion). If omitted, auto-creates a new scene (may fail if scene count cache is stale). Returns { sceneIndex, clipCount } (optimistic — note writes are deferred across multiple flush cycles). To verify, use clip/select + clip/getNotes on individual clips after a few seconds.

sceneIndex.description: Optional bank-relative scene slot index (0–4). If provided, skips scene creation and uses this slot directly. The scene must already exist and be visible in the current scene bank window. Recommended after manual scene creation or bulk deletion.

clips.description: Array of clip definitions, one per track.

notes.description: Array of note objects. Supports optional expression properties.

expressions.description: Per-note expressions {pan, timbre, pressure, gain, transpose, releaseVelocity, velocitySpread, mute}.

post.description: Create and rename multiple scenes in one call, with each rename deferred to a separate flush cycle to avoid Bitwig's scene bank re-indexing bug (ISS-006). Use this instead of calling scene/create + scene/rename in a loop. Returns { created, renamed } (renamed count is optimistic — renames are deferred).

scenes.description: Array of scene definitions. Each scene will be created (in order) then renamed in a separate flush cycle.

index.description: Bank-relative scene index (0–4) to rename. Must match the position the scene will occupy after creation.

If neither is provided, parameters are applied immediately to the currently selected device (reshape mode). Returns { ok, device, pageCount, paramCount, inserted }.

device.description: Bitwig device name to insert (e.g., 'Polymer'). Mutually exclusive with 'plugin'. Omit both to apply parameters to the currently selected device.

plugin.description: Third-party plugin device to insert. Mutually exclusive with 'device'.

position.description: Where to insert the device in the chain. Default: 'end'.

pages.description: Array of page objects, each with pageIndex and params to set on that page.

params.description: Parameters to set on this page.

index.description: Parameter index within the page (0-7).

sections.description: Array of section definitions. Each section is built after all tracks complete. Uses macro/buildSection format.

sceneIndex.description: Optional explicit scene index. If omitted, a new scene is created.

clips.description: Clips to write in this section.

notes.description: Notes to write. Supports optional expression properties.
